verdicts.tldr: The bls12381 gas rows scale M4 Pro timings by a factor measured for a slower Ryzen, so they charge 1.1-1.28x less than the table's own method projects, and regenerating the table will not correct them.
verdicts.details: native_gas.go:193-197 charges the M4 Pro figures times 2.3, while the only 2.3 the table documents is the Ryzen 7 7840U-to-Xeon factor at ibc_native_bench_test.go:77-85. On this Ryzen 7 7840HS, the PR's own BenchmarkFastAggregateVerify takes 1.10x the M4 figure at 1 key and 1.22x at 512 keys (the finder's bench gives 1.20x and 1.28x). So taking a Ryzen measurement and applying 2.3, the table's own method, projects these calls 1.1-1.28x above what the rows charge. The 7840HS is the same Zen 4 Phoenix part as the 7840U at a higher power limit; that the 7840U is no faster is an inference. The ADR says the table is regenerated on the reference machine, but that does not reach these rows: gen_native_table.py and ibc_native_bench_test.go cover cometbls and have no bls12381 spec or bench. A regeneration therefore keeps the M4-derived numbers, which sit below the safety margin every other IBC row got. Fix: measure the bls12381 natives on the 7840U-class host where the 2.3 factor was taken, or on the Xeon, and scale that measurement, or cite the source of an M4-to-Xeon factor in the comment and the ADR.

The shipped row projects by 2.3'. git grep -i bls gnovm/cmd/calibrate finds only cometbls (gen_native_table.py:225, ibc_native_bench_test.go:433).

verdicts.angle: topic: aggregate not a plain sum / equivalence claim
verdicts.tldr: Excluding rejects a valid signature from a committee whose keys sum to the identity, although both docs say it equals FastAggregateVerify over the signers.
verdicts.details: bls12381.go:86 refuses an aggregate that decodes to the identity before subtracting excluded. A committee whose keys sum to the identity therefore can never verify. Example: {pk, -pk}, both valid keys, each able to prove possession because -sk is a valid secret. With excluded [-pk] and pk's signature, Excluding returns false while FastAggregateVerify over the signer [pk] returns true. Both docs promise the opposite: bls12381.go:67-69 states the equivalence, and bls12381.gno:44-45 calls Excluding 'FastAggregateVerify over aggregate minus excluded', with 'a committee in which nobody signed' as the only false case. The cost is a false rejection only, never a forgery. A randomly sampled Ethereum sync committee that holds honest keys does not sum to the identity, and a caller can fall back to FastAggregateVerify over the signers. The PR's own test lists an identity aggregate under 'malformed' (bls12381_test.go:205), so the refusal looks intended and it is the docs that overstate. Fix: either drop '|| agg.IsInfinity()' at line 86, since verifyAggregate already refuses an identity signers' key at line 116, or add the identity-sum committee to the documented false cases in both docs.
verdicts.evidence: At fd7e75152, finder's file added through go test -overlay (git status empty before and after): go test -run 'TestTopic5IdentitySumCommittee$' -v -timeout 2m ./gnovm/stdlibs/crypto/bls12381/ -> 'committee {pk,-pk} aggregate is identity: true', 'FAV over signers [pk]=true, Excluding(agg={pk,-pk}, excl [-pk])=false', '--- FAIL: TestTopic5IdentitySumCommittee'. bls12381.go:86: 'if _, err := agg.SetBytes(aggregate); err != nil || agg.IsInfinity() {'. bls12381.go:67-69: 'It equals FastAggregateVerify over the signers' keys when aggregate is the sum of the committee's keys'. bls12381_test.go:205: require.False(t, X_fastAggregateVerifyExcluding(ib[:], excluded, msg, sig)) under 'malformed'. Not run here: the build with the clause deleted (a read judge makes no mutation; the finder reports it green) and the finder's Ethereum consensus-spec citation.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -run TestTopic5IdentitySumCommittee -v ./gnovm/stdlibs/crypto/bls12381/ with tests/topic5-edge-semantics_test.go copied in: expect FAV true and Excluding false; then delete '|| agg.IsInfinity()' at line 86 and rerun TestTopic5 and TestFastAggregateVerifyExcluding: all green

verdicts.tldr: The ADR's Decision says the package adds one native, but it ships two, and the second is named in the obligations paragraph before line 49 introduces it.
verdicts.details: Line 15 opens the Decision with 'Add crypto/bls12381 with one native, FastAggregateVerify(...)', and the title reads 'BLS signature verification native'. bls12381.go defines two natives. Lines 30 and 35 already state obligations for FastAggregateVerifyExcluding, and the Gas paragraph (42-47) prices only the pubkeys row. Only then does line 49 introduce 'A second native'. Lines 55-57 make that second native the one the light client relies on. A reader of the Decision and Gas paragraphs counts one native and one gas row, then meets a function they were never introduced to. Fix: open the Decision with both natives, FastAggregateVerify and FastAggregateVerifyExcluding, and move the second native's paragraph ahead of Gas so that both rows are priced in one place.
